promise: A 30-day plan built around your goal, one short lesson a day, and a quiz that makes it stick.
need: The Learn AI in 30 Days zip pack from this page
A time of day you can keep, and a note app for your progress log
forTech: The pack is a tutor prompt plus a plan file and a progress log. The model reads the log at the start of each session and quizzes you on earlier days before it teaches anything new. That's retrieval practice with spaced review.
intro: You've saved the videos. You've read the threads. You still don't know where to start, because every expert starts from a different place and none of them start from yours.
Watching doesn't teach you. Doing one small thing a day, then being asked about it the next day, does. What I know about AI comes from using it on real work in my own business every day.
This pack turns Claude or ChatGPT into a patient teacher. It builds a 30-day plan around one goal you pick. It teaches one thing a day, has you try it on something real, and quizzes you so it sticks.

body: The zip has a file called START_HERE.md. It's written to the AI, not to you. It tells Claude or ChatGPT how to teach you.

steps.title: Pick one goal
steps.text: Not "learn AI". Pick something you can see, like "use AI to write my weekly report" or "build a helper for my inbox". The plan gets built around it.
steps.why: A goal you can see keeps you coming back on day 9.

steps.title: Give the pack a home
steps.text: Unzip it. In Claude or ChatGPT, make a new project and add all the files. If you don't have projects, open one new chat, attach the files, and keep coming back to that same chat.

steps.title: Start Day 1
steps.copy: Read START_HERE.md and follow it exactly. Use the files in the templates folder. I'm starting Day 1.

body: Day 1 is an interview. No lesson yet.

steps.title: Answer the questions
steps.text: It asks about your goal, your work, what you've tried, and how many minutes a day you really have. Be honest about the minutes. A small number you keep beats a big one you don't.

steps.title: Read the plan and push back
steps.text: You get 4 weeks on one page. If a week looks too easy, too hard or not useful for your goal, say so. It'll change it. Then save the plan.

body: Every day after that has the same 4 parts: a short quiz on earlier days, one new idea, one thing to try on your own real work, and one line for your log.
The quiz comes first on purpose. Pulling an answer out of your head is what makes it stay there.

steps.title: Open each day the same way
steps.text: Paste your progress log and send this.
steps.copy:
Day [number]. Here is my progress log:

[paste your log]

Quiz me on earlier days first. Then teach me today's lesson.

steps.title: Do the try-it task
steps.text: Every lesson ends with one small thing to do on your own work. Do it before you close the chat. Reading isn't the lesson. The task is.

steps.title: Save your new log
steps.text: At the end it gives you an updated log. Copy it into your notes.
steps.why: A chat can forget. Your log doesn't.

sections.h: When life gets in the way
body: You'll miss a day. Everyone does. The plan bends.

steps.title: If you missed some days
steps.text: Don't start over, and don't try to do 4 lessons in one night.
steps.copy:
I missed some days. My last finished day was Day [number]. Here is my progress log:

[paste your log]

Don't make me cram. Adjust the plan from here and start with a short review quiz.

steps.title: If a lesson doesn't land
steps.text: Ask again. A good teacher has more than one way to say it.
steps.copy: I didn't get that. Explain it again like I'm 12, with an example from my job. Then ask me one question to check I got it.

steps.title: Day 30: build one thing
steps.text: The last day is a small project for your goal. You build it, the AI reviews it with you, and you keep it.

eureka: I don't learn AI by watching. I learn it by doing one small thing a day and getting quizzed on it.
check: You have a 30-day plan built around one goal, saved where you'll find it
You have a time of day set for your lesson
You did the Day 1 interview and your first try-it task
Your progress log has at least one line in it
limits: It teaches you to use AI well. It doesn't build agents for you.
It only knows what's in your log. If you don't paste the log, it starts from zero.
AI tools change often. If a lesson doesn't match your screen, tell it what you see and it'll adjust.
It doesn't know your company's rules on AI. Check those before you use it on work files.

diy.line: Once you know the basics, Your First AI Team at Work is the free guide that gives you 3 helpers to build: inbox, meeting notes and a Friday report.

dwy.line: A Strategy Call is 60 minutes with me, and you can use it for training on advanced AI once the basics are solid.

dfy.line: If you run a business and would sooner have the agents built than learn to build them, every build starts with the Discovery Call.
